meta.description: Tests whether GWAS and molecular-QTL signals share a causal variant, using coloc.abf, coloc.susie, SMR/HEIDI, and documented multi-trait or conditional alternatives.
meta.reaudit_of: Report and run evidence archived at F:/OpenScience/audits/_pre-fix-20260922/bio-causal-genomics-colocalization-analysis/ before this audit.
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md

scientific_integrity.detail: All numerical results in Inputs 1-10 were generated from explicitly labelled synthetic data with planted truth; no result is represented as clinical or population evidence.

practice_boundaries.detail: The Skill and all outputs are research-statistics workflows. They make no individual diagnosis or treatment recommendation.

methodological_ground.detail: Input 10 supplied eQTL z-scores incompatible with the LD matrix (independently measured eQTL lambda=1.000000). scripts/coloc_susie.R checks only GWAS lambda, continues, and prints a PP.H4=1 result instead of stopping. This defeats the stated two-trait LD-mismatch safeguard and can support a false colocalization conclusion.

code_usability.detail: All nine shipped R files parse. Inputs 1-9 completed and wrote checked outputs. The shared Windows R wrapper returned 139 after several fully materialized coloc outputs, but the produced result files and independent assertions were valid; this seat-level post-output status is reported as a P1 reliability issue, not treated as successful exit-code evidence.

functional_suitability.note: Broad method coverage and decision routing are strong, but the documented coloc.susie LD-mismatch safeguard is only implemented for GWAS, not eQTL, which is a core correctness gap.

reliability.note: MHC and chromosome-8 hard stops, harmonisation, and most failure-mode guidance are explicit. The missing eQTL lambda stop permits an invalid LD pairing to continue.

performance_context.note: The 273-line SKILL.md routes detailed method material into focused references and scripts without unnecessary upfront loading.

agent_usability.note: The decision tree, command forms, expected files, version checks, and reporting requirements are precise and consistent.

human_usability.note: Natural trigger wording and strict scientific-input requirements are clear; strict stops correctly protect data integrity.

security.note: No credentials, destructive operations, or sensitive-data retention are required by the shipped workflow.

maintainability.note: The reference/script split and parseable R sources are maintainable, but the duplicated conceptual LD check was not exercised as a two-trait contract and lacks a shipped regression test.

agent_specific.note: Trigger precision, composability, idempotent file-oriented scripts, and exclusion-region escape hatches are excellent.

key_strengths: All prior regression inputs plus two new positive-control source-script inputs ran on the requested exact commit with output assertions.
The current shipped SuSiE examples recover their planted truth and the new harmonisation complement branch is verified.
MHC and chromosome-8 exclusions, coloc.abf output materialization, SMR/HEIDI controls, and regional plotting were independently exercised.
The 2026-09-21 source split gives the workflow focused references and directly runnable scripts.

recommendations.title: Check eQTL LD mismatch before coloc.susie
recommendations.problem: scripts/coloc_susie.R checks estimate_s_rss only for GWAS. An eQTL LD mismatch with lambda=1.0 continued and printed PP.H4=1.
recommendations.root_cause: The two-trait diagnostic was implemented for z_gwas but never repeated for eQTL z-scores.
recommendations.fix: Compute z_eqtl and lam_eqtl with the supplied LD and eQTL N immediately after the GWAS check. Stop when either lambda exceeds --lambda-max, and add a shipped regression test proving the eQTL-only mismatch fails before runsusie or coloc.susie.

recommendations.title: Exercise documented alternative-method branches
recommendations.problem: moloc, eCAVIAR, and PWCoCo remain unexecuted in this Phase 2 evidence set because their required package or compiled binaries are absent from the shared environment. HyPrColoc was not independently re-run in this Phase 2 audit.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill documents more methods than the current reproducible environment provides.
recommendations.fix: Install or build each tool in an isolated environment, run a planted 3-trait moloc case, an allelic-heterogeneity eCAVIAR case, a COJO/PWCoCo conditional case, and a multi-trait HyPrColoc case; retain scripts and assertions.

recommendations.title: Resolve post-output Windows R exit 139
recommendations.problem: This shared Windows R wrapper returned status 139 after several coloc runs despite complete files and correct printed results.
recommendations.root_cause: Likely an environment or binary interaction rather than source-script logic, but a nonzero process status makes unattended use unreliable.
recommendations.fix: Reproduce with a minimal coloc script outside the audit harness, identify the R or native-package layer, and either repair the environment or document a supported runtime whose successful outputs also exit zero.
